issues.current_text: A Organização Marítima Internacional reportou 3.200 navios com 20 mil marinheiros presos a oeste de Hormuz... O Brent ultrapassou $106 o barril — 40% acima do nível pré-guerra — e a Agência Internacional de Energia classificou o fechamento como 'a maior disrupção no fornecimento de energia da história'
issues.previous_text: mais de 3 mil navios e 20 mil marinheiros seguem presos no Golfo Pérsico... Brent fechou a US$103,14. A IEA classificou Hormuz como 'a maior interrupção de oferta da história do mercado de petróleo'
issues.suggestion: The Hormuz ship count (3,000→3,200) and IEA 'biggest disruption' quote have appeared in 3 consecutive editions. Cut the IEA quote entirely — readers have seen it. Lead with what's NEW: the IMO emergency session on March 18-19, Trump's failed coalition (no country confirmed ships), and India's independent escort operation. The price update ($106) is fine as a data point but don't re-explain the 'biggest disruption' framing.

issues.previous_text: mais de 3 mil navios e 20 mil marinheiros seguem presos (03-14); mais de 3 mil navios e 20 mil marinheiros seguem presos (03-15)
issues.suggestion: Third consecutive edition with nearly identical 'X mil navios com 20 mil marinheiros presos' construction. If keeping the stat, fold it into a subordinate clause ('com o número de navios retidos subindo para 3.200') rather than giving it headline treatment again.

issues.current_text: 288 GB de HBM4, 336 bilhões de transistores e 50 petaFLOPS de inferência FP4 por chip — 5x o desempenho e 10x a redução de custo por token sobre o Blackwell Ultra
issues.previous_text: plataforma Rubin com 288 GB de HBM4 e até 50 petaFLOPS
issues.suggestion: The Vera Rubin specs (288 GB HBM4, 50 petaFLOPS) were already previewed on 03-14. Since this is the actual announcement, keep the specs but acknowledge they were leaked/previewed. Better yet, focus on the NEW information: the $1T pipeline projection, Micron HBM4 mass production, the Feynman 2028 roadmap, and Groq 3 LPU — these are all genuinely new and more interesting than rehashing the spec sheet.

issues.current_text: NemoClaw ganhou corpo: camada de segurança e privacidade para o OpenClaw
issues.suggestion: NemoClaw was introduced yesterday. Today's coverage adds real detail (OpenShell sandbox, GeForce to DGX range), which is good. But the name drop feels repetitive to daily readers. Consider leading with the functional capability ('Nvidia shipped a local-first agent sandbox from GeForce to DGX') rather than re-introducing the product name as if it's new.

issues.current_text: Mira Murati saiu do painel de ontem para anunciar parceria de escala gigawatt entre seu Thinking Machines Lab e a Nvidia para treinar modelos frontier com Vera Rubin
issues.previous_text: Mira Murati, agora na Thinking Machines Lab
issues.suggestion: Murati/Thinking Machines Lab was mentioned yesterday. Today there's a genuine new development (gigawatt partnership with Nvidia). The 'saiu do painel de ontem' phrasing helpfully signals continuity — this one is fine as-is.

issues.current_text: a Agência Internacional de Energia classificou o fechamento como 'a maior disrupção no fornecimento de energia da história'
issues.previous_text: A IEA classificou Hormuz como 'a maior interrupção de oferta da história do mercado de petróleo'
issues.suggestion: Same IEA quote paraphrased slightly differently. Cut it — it ran two days ago. Readers remember.

issues.current_text: petróleo ultrapassa $106 com 3.200 navios presos em Hormuz (subtitle); entire paragraph on Hormuz ships + oil price + IEA quote + coalition diplomacy
issues.previous_text: na véspera da GTC... 3 mil navios presos mantêm o Brent acima de US$103 (03-14 subtitle); Hormuz fechado com Brent a $100 (03-13 subtitle)
issues.suggestion: Four consecutive editions frame Hormuz the same way: escalating oil price + ship count + superlative IEA quote. The reader sees the same graph going up every day. Reframe around a DIFFERENT angle: the diplomatic failure (no country confirmed joining Trump's coalition), India going solo, or the downstream consequences (Cuba blackout was partly caused by Venezuelan oil being cut). The Cuba blackout paragraph already provides a fresh angle — consider leading the geopolitical section with Cuba/energy consequences rather than the Hormuz update.

issues.current_text: Israel eliminou dois chefes de inteligência iranianos em Teerã como parte de 20 ondas de ataques sobre 150 alvos
issues.previous_text: Israel completou 20 ondas de ataques em 24 horas contra mais de 200 alvos
issues.suggestion: The '20 ondas de ataques' framing appeared on 03-13. While these may be different attack waves, the identical phrasing ('20 ondas') makes it feel like a copy-paste. If these are new waves, clarify ('mais 20 ondas' or give a cumulative count). If it's the same campaign, drop the wave count and focus on the new intel: the intelligence chiefs killed and the Khamenei aircraft destroyed.

issues.current_text: Three-day GTC arc: preview specs (03-14) → conference opens (03-15) → keynote recap (03-16)
issues.previous_text: GTC covered in 03-14 (silicon shortage + Vera Rubin specs), 03-15 (GTC opens, NemoClaw, Murati panel)
issues.suggestion: Three days of GTC coverage risks reader fatigue. Today's edition correctly focuses on the keynote announcements, but the Vera Rubin specs and NemoClaw were already covered. Tighten the GTC section: lead with the $1T pipeline (genuinely shocking number), the Feynman 2028 roadmap, and the Disney Olaf robot (fun, memorable). Move repeated specs to parenthetical references. The LangChain and Mistral paragraphs are NOT GTC-related and could be separated to break the Nvidia monotony.

summary: High repetition on Hormuz/oil (same framing 4 days running) and moderate repetition on GTC/Vera Rubin specs (previewed 2 days ago). The IEA 'biggest disruption' quote and ship count should be cut or compressed. Fresh angles exist (Cuba blackout, India solo escort, diplomatic failure) but are buried under the same escalation narrative.
